Using a muddler or the end of a wooden spoon, press and twist the lime pieces firmly against the bottom and sides of the glass for about 20-30 seconds, until you've released plenty of juice and the sugar has mostly dissolved into it.
Fill the glass with ice cubes.
Pour in 2 oz cachaça over the ice.
Stir well with a spoon for a few seconds to combine everything, then serve immediately with a short straw, leaving the muddled lime pieces in the glass.

dishes.name: Yerba Mate
dishes.description: Traditional caffeinated infusion shared communally through a metal straw.
steps: Fill a gourd about two-thirds full with yerba mate leaves.
Tilt the gourd to let the leaves settle to one side.
Insert the metal straw (bombilla) into the empty side.
Pour hot, not boiling, water slowly over the leaves.
Sip through the straw, refilling with hot water as it's finished, traditionally shared among a group.

dishes.name: Ayran
dishes.description: Savory, salted yogurt drink popular across Turkey and the Balkans.
steps: In a large bowl or pitcher, combine 2 cups plain yogurt and 2 cups cold water.
Whisk vigorously (or use a blender on low speed) until the mixture is completely smooth and no lumps of yogurt remain, about 1-2 minutes.
Add 1/2 teaspoon salt and whisk again until fully dissolved.
Taste and adjust the salt to your liking - ayran should taste refreshingly salty-tangy, not sweet.
Cover and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes; it separates slightly as it sits, so whisk it once more right before serving.
Pour into glasses over a few ice cubes and serve very cold.

dishes.name: Kvass
dishes.description: Mildly alcoholic fermented rye bread beverage, a Slavic staple.
steps: Toast or dry out rye bread pieces in a low oven until very dark.
Steep the toasted bread in hot water for several hours.
Strain the liquid, then stir in sugar and a small amount of yeast.
Let ferment at room temperature for 1-2 days until lightly fizzy and tangy.
Strain again, bottle, and chill before serving.

dishes.name: Horchata
dishes.description: Sweet, milky rice and cinnamon drink served chilled.
steps: Place 1 cup rice and a cinnamon stick in a bowl or jar, and cover with 4 cups water.
Cover and let it soak at room temperature for at least 4 hours, or ideally overnight in the refrigerator - the rice will soften and the water will take on a faint cinnamon flavor.
Pour the soaked rice, cinnamon stick, and soaking water into a blender. Blend on high for 1-2 minutes, until as smooth as possible (it won't be perfectly smooth, since rice doesn't fully break down).
Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth, or a nut milk bag, pressing and squeezing to extract as much liquid as possible. Discard the solids left behind.
Stir 1/2 cup sweetened condensed milk and 1 teaspoon vanilla into the strained liquid until fully combined.
Chill well in the refrigerator for at least an hour, then stir again and serve over ice.

dishes.name: Turkish Coffee
dishes.description: Unfiltered coffee brewed slowly in a small pot, served with the grounds settled at the bottom.
steps: Combine finely ground coffee, cold water, and sugar (if using) in a small pot (cezve).
Stir well before heating.
Heat slowly over low heat, without stirring once it's on the heat.
Just as it begins to foam and rise, remove from heat, let it settle, then return briefly to heat once or twice more.
Pour into small cups, letting the grounds settle before drinking.

dishes.name: Moroccan Mint Tea
dishes.description: Sweet green tea steeped with fresh mint, poured from height to create froth.
steps: Rinse the green tea leaves briefly with a little boiling water, then discard that water.
Add fresh mint and sugar to the teapot with the tea leaves.
Pour in boiling water and let steep for 5 minutes.
Stir well to dissolve the sugar.
Pour from a height into small glasses to create a light froth.

dishes.name: Pisco Sour
dishes.description: Frothy South American cocktail built on grape brandy.
steps: Add 2 oz pisco, 1 oz lime juice, 3/4 oz simple syrup, and 1 egg white to a cocktail shaker.
Seal the shaker and shake vigorously without ice for about 15-20 seconds (this is called a 'dry shake') - this step is essential, as it's what emulsifies the egg white into a creamy foam.
Open the shaker, add a generous handful of ice, and shake again vigorously for another 15 seconds, until the outside of the shaker feels very cold.
Strain the mixture into a chilled glass, straining out the ice, so you're left with a smooth, frothy drink topped with a layer of foam.
Let the drink sit for a few seconds to allow the foam to settle on top.
Add 2 dashes of bitters directly onto the foam - traditionally you can drag a toothpick through the drops to create a decorative pattern. Serve immediately.

dishes.name: Michelada
dishes.description: Spicy, savory beer cocktail popular as a hangover cure.
steps: Pour a shallow layer of chili powder and salt onto a small plate, mixing them together.
Wet the rim of a tall glass by running a lime wedge around the outer edge, then dip the rim into the chili-salt mixture, turning it to coat evenly. Set the glass upright.
Fill the glass about two-thirds full with ice.
Add 1 oz lime juice, 1 teaspoon hot sauce, and 1/2 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce directly into the glass over the ice.
Slowly pour in the cold lager beer, tilting the glass slightly to reduce foam, filling almost to the top.
Give it one gentle stir with a spoon or straw (don't stir hard, or you'll lose the fizz) and serve immediately.

dishes.name: Rooibos Tea
dishes.description: Naturally caffeine-free red tea native to South Africa.
steps: Bring 2 cups water to a full rolling boil in a kettle or small pot.
Place 2 teaspoons rooibos leaves into a teapot or a tea infuser/strainer set inside a cup.
Pour the boiling water over the rooibos leaves.
Let it steep for a full 5-7 minutes (longer than you would steep black or green tea) - rooibos is naturally caffeine-free and mild, so it needs more time to release its flavor and reddish color.
Strain the tea into cups, removing the loose leaves or infuser.
Add milk and honey to taste, if desired, and stir before serving warm.

dishes.name: Chicha Morada
dishes.description: Sweet, spiced Peruvian drink made from purple corn.
steps: Rinse the dried purple corn (kernels and cob if using) under cold water to remove any dust.
In a large pot, combine the purple corn, pineapple rind, cinnamon stick, and cloves with about 8-10 cups of water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 45-60 minutes, until the water has turned a deep, vivid purple and reduced slightly.
Strain the liquid through a fine sieve into a large pitcher or bowl, pressing on the solids to extract as much liquid and flavor as possible, then discard the solids.
While the liquid is still warm, stir in sugar to taste until fully dissolved — it dissolves more easily in warm liquid than cold.
Stir in fresh lime juice, tasting and adjusting the balance of sweet and tart to your liking.
Let the chicha morada cool to room temperature, then refrigerate until thoroughly chilled, at least 2-3 hours.
Serve very cold over ice, with a few chunks of fresh diced fruit (apple or pineapple) stirred in if you like.

dishes.name: Onigiri
dishes.description: Hand-formed rice balls wrapped in seaweed, a Japanese lunchbox staple.
steps: Cook the rice with slightly less water than usual so it's a bit firmer and stickier than typical steamed rice — this helps the onigiri hold its shape. Let it cool just until warm enough to handle comfortably, not hot.
Prepare your filling: flake cooked salmon into small pieces, or have your pickled plum (umeboshi) or tuna mayo ready in a small bowl.
Fill a small bowl with water and stir in a pinch of salt — this is what you'll wet your hands with.
Wet your hands thoroughly with the salted water (this seasons the rice slightly and, importantly, keeps it from sticking to your palms).
Take a handful of warm rice (about 1/2 cup) and flatten it into a disc in your palm. Make a small well in the center and add a spoonful of filling.

Add a little more rice on top to cover the filling completely, then cup your hands around it and press firmly but gently, shaping it into a triangle by rotating and pressing the edges with the heel of your hand three times.
Repeat with the remaining rice and filling, re-wetting your hands with salted water between each onigiri to prevent sticking.
Wrap a strip of nori around the base of each onigiri just before eating (wrapping too far ahead makes the nori go soft and chewy instead of crisp).

dishes.name: Chirashi Don
dishes.description: Bowl of sushi rice scattered with an assortment of fresh sashimi.
steps: Cook the sushi rice: rinse until the water runs clear, then cook with a slightly reduced water ratio for firmer grains. While still hot, fold in a mixture of rice vinegar, sugar, and salt, fanning the rice as you fold to help it cool quickly and turn glossy.
Spread the seasoned rice into serving bowls in an even layer and let it cool to room temperature (chirashi is best with rice that's cooled, not hot).
Slice your sashimi-grade fish (tuna, salmon, yellowtail, etc.) into clean, even pieces about 1/4-inch thick, using a sharp knife in single smooth strokes rather than sawing.

Arrange the sliced fish artfully over the rice, along with any other toppings like tamago (sweet omelet), cucumber, avocado, or ikura (salmon roe), grouping colors and textures so the bowl looks vibrant and varied.
Garnish with thin strips of nori, a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds, and a small mound of wasabi and pickled ginger on the side.
Serve immediately with soy sauce for drizzling or dipping.

dishes.name: Yakisoba
dishes.description: Stir-fried wheat noodles in a tangy-sweet sauce, popular festival food.
steps: Stir-fry sliced pork until cooked through.
Add shredded cabbage and any other vegetables, cooking until just tender.
Add the noodles directly to the pan with a splash of water to loosen them.
Pour in the yakisoba sauce and toss everything together until evenly coated.
Top with pickled ginger before serving.

dishes.name: Oyakodon
dishes.description: Chicken and egg simmered together over rice; name means 'parent and child bowl'.
steps: Thinly slice the chicken thigh into bite-sized pieces and thinly slice the onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together dashi (or water with a pinch of dashi powder), soy sauce, mirin, and a little sugar to make the simmering sauce.
Pour the sauce into a small skillet or shallow pan and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly softened.
Add the chicken pieces in a single layer and simmer for 4-5 minutes, until mostly cooked through.
Beat the eggs lightly (don't overbeat — you want streaks of white and yolk, not a uniform mixture) and pour about two-thirds of it evenly over the chicken and onion.
Cover the pan and cook for about 1 minute, then pour in the remaining egg, cover again, and cook for another 30-60 seconds until the eggs are just set but still soft and a little runny in places.
Slide the chicken-and-egg mixture directly on top of a bowl of hot steamed rice, letting any extra sauce soak down into the rice.
Garnish with sliced scallions and serve immediately while the egg is still warm and glossy.

dishes.name: Samgyeopsal
dishes.description: Thick-cut pork belly grilled at the table and wrapped in lettuce.
steps: Heat a grill or heavy pan until very hot.
Grill the thick pork belly slices, turning occasionally, until crisp outside and cooked through.
Grill sliced garlic alongside for a few minutes.
Snip the cooked pork into bite-sized pieces with kitchen scissors.
Wrap pieces in lettuce with garlic and a dab of ssamjang to eat.

dishes.name: Sundubu Jjigae
dishes.description: Bubbling, spicy soft tofu stew served in a stone pot.
steps: Sauté pork or seafood with gochugaru in a little oil until fragrant.
Add water or stock and bring to a simmer.
Spoon in the soft tofu in large chunks without stirring too much.
Simmer until everything is cooked through, about 8 minutes.
Crack an egg into the center just before serving, letting the residual heat cook it.

dishes.name: Sichuan Hot Pot
dishes.description: Communal simmering pot of fiery, numbing broth for cooking meat and vegetables tableside.
steps: Bring the prepared hot pot broth to a simmer in a pot at the center of the table.
Arrange thinly sliced meats and vegetables on platters around the pot.
Each diner cooks their own ingredients briefly in the simmering broth using chopsticks or a strainer.
Dip cooked items in the sesame-garlic sauce before eating.
Continue adding ingredients to the pot throughout the meal.

dishes.name: Xinjiang Lamb Skewers
dishes.description: Cumin-and-chili-crusted grilled lamb skewers from China's Xinjiang region.
steps: Cut the lamb into 1-inch cubes, keeping a little fat on some pieces for flavor and juiciness. Thread the cubes onto skewers, packing them fairly close together.
In a small bowl, mix ground cumin, chili flakes, salt, and a little sugar to make the signature dry spice rub.
If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 20 minutes beforehand to prevent burning.
Heat a grill, grill pan, or broiler to high heat. Just before cooking, sprinkle the skewers generously with the cumin-chili spice mix on all sides, pressing it on so it sticks.
Grill the skewers for 2-3 minutes per side (8-10 minutes total), turning to char all sides, until the lamb is browned and slightly crisp on the outside but still juicy inside.
Just before removing from the heat, sprinkle another light dusting of the cumin-chili mix over the skewers for an extra hit of flavor and aroma.
Serve immediately while hot, straight off the skewers.

dishes.name: Cantonese Roast Goose
dishes.description: Crackling-skinned roast goose, a Cantonese specialty.
steps: Season the goose cavity generously with five-spice.
Blanch the skin briefly with boiling water, then air-dry uncovered in the fridge for several hours.
Brush the skin with a glaze of maltose, vinegar, and soy sauce.
Roast at high heat, turning as needed, until the skin is deep mahogany and crackling.
Rest before carving into thin slices.

dishes.name: Macher Jhol
dishes.description: Bengali light fish curry, a staple of everyday Bengali meals.
steps: Rub fish steaks with turmeric and a little salt, then lightly fry in mustard oil until golden, and set aside.
In the same oil, fry potato cubes until lightly browned.
Add tomato and a light spice blend, cooking until it forms a thin sauce.
Add water and bring to a simmer, then return the fish to the pan.
Simmer gently until the fish is cooked through and the potatoes are tender.

dishes.name: Litti Chokha
dishes.description: Bihar's rustic dish of roasted stuffed wheat balls with mashed vegetables.
steps: Make a stiff wheat dough and rest it.
Mix sattu with mustard oil, spices, and a little water to make the filling.
Stuff dough balls with the sattu filling and seal well.
Roast over an open flame or bake until the crust is browned and slightly cracked.
Mash roasted eggplant and potato with mustard oil and spices, and serve alongside.

dishes.name: Sarson ka Saag
dishes.description: Punjabi mustard greens curry, classically paired with cornbread.
steps: Simmer mustard greens and spinach in a little water until very soft.
Blend the cooked greens with ginger into a coarse puree.
Return to the pot and stir in cornmeal to thicken slightly.
Simmer another 10 minutes, stirring often.
Finish with a generous knob of butter and serve with makki di roti.

dishes.name: Rasam
dishes.description: Thin, peppery South Indian soup often eaten with rice.
steps: Heat oil or ghee in a pot over medium heat. Add mustard seeds and let them pop, then add cumin seeds, curry leaves, and a dried red chili, frying for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add minced garlic and cook for another 30 seconds, then stir in tamarind pulp (or tamarind concentrate mixed with water) along with chopped tomato.
Add rasam powder (or a mix of ground coriander, cumin, black pepper, and turmeric) and stir to combine, letting the spices bloom in the fat for a minute.
Pour in water and bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes, letting the tomato break down and the flavors meld into a thin, tangy, aromatic broth.
If using, stir in cooked lentils (toor dal) mashed smooth, which thickens the rasam slightly and adds body.
Season with salt to taste, and simmer for another 5 minutes until the broth is fragrant and well balanced between tangy, spicy, and savory.
Just before serving, add a final tempering if you like an extra flavor boost: quickly fry more mustard seeds and curry leaves in a small pan of hot ghee and pour it sizzling over the rasam.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot, either as a soup on its own or poured over steamed rice.

dishes.name: Payasam
dishes.description: South Indian sweet milk pudding, served at festivals.
steps: Toast vermicelli or rice lightly in a little ghee.
Add milk and simmer until the vermicelli or rice is fully cooked and the milk has thickened.
Stir in jaggery or sugar until dissolved.
Add cardamom for fragrance.
Fry cashews and raisins in ghee and stir in just before serving, warm or chilled.

dishes.name: Bánh Xèo
dishes.description: Crispy Vietnamese savory crepe folded around shrimp and pork.
steps: Mix rice flour batter with turmeric for color.
Sauté shrimp and pork in a hot pan, then pour in a thin layer of batter.
Add bean sprouts on one half of the crepe.
Cook until the edges are crisp and lacy, then fold in half like an omelet.
Serve with lettuce and herbs for wrapping, plus a dipping sauce.

dishes.name: Cao Lầu
dishes.description: Regional Vietnamese noodle dish unique to the town of Hoi An.
steps: Prepare thick, chewy rice noodles (traditionally made with a specific local water).
Braise or roast pork until tender and flavorful, then slice thinly.
Toss the noodles with a small amount of the pork braising liquid.
Top with sliced pork, fresh greens, and crispy fried noodle croutons.
Serve with just a small amount of broth, unlike a full noodle soup.

dishes.name: Mango Sticky Rice
dishes.description: Sweet coconut sticky rice served with ripe mango slices.
steps: Soak glutinous rice for several hours, then steam until tender and translucent.
Warm coconut milk with sugar and a pinch of salt until dissolved.
Pour most of the coconut mixture over the hot steamed rice and let it absorb.
Slice ripe mango.
Serve the rice alongside mango slices, drizzled with the remaining coconut sauce.

dishes.name: Tom Kha Gai
dishes.description: Creamy, tangy coconut chicken soup, milder than tom yum.
steps: Prep the aromatics: bruise the lemongrass stalks with the back of a knife and cut into 2-inch lengths, and slice the galangal into thin coins. This releases their oils for infusing.

Pour the coconut milk into a pot (reserve a splash of the thicker cream from the top if you can) and add the galangal and lemongrass. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat — don't let it boil hard, or the coconut milk can split.
Let the aromatics infuse for 5-7 minutes so the broth takes on their fragrance, then add the sliced chicken in a single layer.
Simmer gently for 6-8 minutes, until the chicken is just cooked through and no longer pink in the center.
Season with fish sauce (start with 2-3 tablespoons) and a pinch of sugar, tasting and adjusting — the balance should be salty, a little sweet, and about to turn sour.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the fresh lime juice — adding it off-heat keeps the flavor bright instead of bitter.
Taste and adjust: add more fish sauce for saltiness, lime for tang, or a sliced fresh chili for heat.
Ladle into bowls, discarding the woody lemongrass and galangal pieces if you like (or leave them in for aroma, just don't eat them), and garnish with torn cilantro leaves and thin chili slices.

dishes.name: Soto Ayam
dishes.description: Indonesian turmeric-spiced chicken soup.
steps: Simmer chicken with turmeric, lemongrass, and aromatics until tender.
Remove chicken, shred it, and strain the broth.
Cook vermicelli separately.
Assemble bowls with vermicelli, shredded chicken, and sliced boiled egg.
Ladle the hot turmeric broth over the top and garnish with fried shallots.

dishes.name: Rawon
dishes.description: Dark, earthy East Javanese beef stew colored by black nuts.
steps: Brown beef cubes with onion and aromatics.
Stir in black keluak paste, giving the dish its distinctive dark color.
Add tamarind and enough water to cover, then simmer until the beef is tender, about 1.5 hours.
Season to balance the earthy, tangy flavor.
Serve with rice and fresh bean sprouts on top.

dishes.name: Bicol Express
dishes.description: Spicy Filipino pork stew named after a train route, cooked in coconut milk.
steps: Heat a couple tablespoons of oil in a wide, heavy pan or wok over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and sliced chili and sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant but not browned.
Add the sliced pork belly and cook, stirring occasionally, for 6-8 minutes until it starts to brown lightly and render some of its fat.
Stir in the shrimp paste and cook for another minute to toast it slightly and mellow its raw funk.
Pour in the coconut milk, stirring to combine everything into a smooth sauce. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered over medium-low heat, stirring every few minutes, for 30-40 minutes until the pork is tender and the sauce has reduced by about half and thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Taste and adjust seasoning — shrimp paste varies in saltiness, so add more only if needed. For extra heat, stir in more sliced chilies in the last 5 minutes.
Serve hot over steamed white rice, spooning plenty of the thickened coconut sauce over each portion.

dishes.name: Tapsilog
dishes.description: Filipino breakfast combo of cured beef, fried rice, and egg.
steps: Heat a little oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the cured beef (tapa) and pan-fry for 3-4 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
In a separate pan, heat a little oil and add minced garlic, cooking for 30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Add the cooked rice to the garlic pan, breaking up any clumps with a spatula, and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes over medium-high heat, until the rice is heated through and slightly crisp in places.
In a third pan (or after removing the beef and garlic rice), fry the eggs sunny-side up for 2-3 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny.
Plate the sliced beef, a mound of garlic rice, and a fried egg together on each plate.
Serve with a small bowl of vinegar-garlic dipping sauce on the side.

dishes.name: Baba Ganoush
dishes.description: Smoky roasted eggplant dip, a Levantine mezze staple.
steps: Char whole eggplants directly over an open flame, turning occasionally, until the skin is completely blackened and blistered and the flesh feels very soft — this smoky char gives baba ganoush its distinctive flavor. Roasting in the oven works as a backup if you don't have an open flame.
Let the charred eggplants cool slightly, then cut them open and scoop the soft flesh into a colander, leaving the skin behind.
Let the flesh drain for about 10 minutes — eggplant holds a surprising amount of liquid, and draining prevents a watery dip.
Transfer to a bowl and mash with a fork, or pulse briefly in a food processor for a smoother texture.
Mix in tahini, minced garlic, and lemon juice.
Taste and adjust — baba ganoush needs a good amount of salt and lemon to taste bright rather than flat.
Spread onto a plate, drizzle generously with olive oil, and serve with warm pita or fresh vegetables.

dishes.name: Manakish
dishes.description: Lebanese flatbread topped with za'atar and olive oil, eaten for breakfast.
steps: In a small bowl, mix 1/2 cup za'atar with about 1/3 cup olive oil, stirring until you get a thick, spreadable, paste-like consistency (add a touch more oil if it seems dry).
Preheat your oven to its highest setting (around 475-500°F/245-260°C), ideally with a baking stone or upside-down baking sheet inside to heat up.
On a lightly floured surface, roll each portion of dough out into a round about 8 inches across and 1/4 inch thick.
Transfer the rounds to a piece of parchment paper or a lightly floured pizza peel. Spread the za'atar-oil mixture generously and evenly over each round, all the way to the edges.

Slide the rounds (on their parchment, or directly if using a peel) onto the hot baking stone or a hot baking sheet, and bake for 8-10 minutes, until the edges are golden-brown and crisp and the center is cooked through.
Remove from the oven, let cool for a minute, and serve warm, often folded in half to eat like a wrap.

dishes.name: Knafeh
dishes.description: Warm, syrup-soaked cheese pastry topped with crushed pistachios.
steps: Toss shredded phyllo with melted butter until evenly coated.
Press half the phyllo into a round pan.
Spread the sweet cheese evenly over the phyllo layer.
Top with the remaining phyllo, pressing down firmly.
Bake until golden, then immediately soak with sugar syrup and top with crushed pistachios.

dishes.name: Falooda
dishes.description: Layered rose-flavored milk dessert with vermicelli and basil seeds.
steps: Cook the vermicelli noodles in boiling water according to the package instructions, usually about 3-5 minutes, until tender. Drain, rinse under cold water, and let cool.
Pour about 2 tablespoons of rose syrup into the bottom of each tall glass, tilting to coat the bottom evenly.
Add a spoonful of soaked basil seeds on top of the syrup, followed by a layer of the cooled cooked vermicelli.
Slowly pour chilled milk down the side of the glass, filling it about three-quarters full, taking care not to disturb the layers too much.
Top with a generous scoop of ice cream.
Drizzle a little extra rose syrup over the top and serve immediately with a long spoon and straw, stirring the layers together as you eat.

dishes.name: Pounded Yam
dishes.description: Smooth, stretchy staple made by pounding boiled yam, eaten with soup.
steps: Boil peeled yam chunks in water until very soft, about 20-25 minutes.
Drain well.
Pound the hot yam in a mortar (or use a stand mixer with a dough hook) until completely smooth and stretchy.
Wet hands or tools periodically to prevent sticking.
Shape into a smooth mound and serve with soup.

dishes.name: Red Red
dishes.description: Ghanaian bean stew named for its red palm oil color, served with fried plantain.
steps: Cook black-eyed peas until tender, about 45 minutes.
Sauté onion in palm oil until soft, then add tomato paste and cook until fragrant.
Combine the cooked beans with the tomato-onion base and simmer 10 minutes.
Fry sliced ripe plantain until caramelized.
Serve the beans with the fried plantain on the side.

dishes.name: Canjeero
dishes.description: Somali spongy fermented flatbread, similar in spirit to injera.
steps: Mix flour, water, yeast, and sugar into a thin batter.
Let it ferment at room temperature for several hours until bubbly.
Heat a lightly oiled non-stick pan.
Pour a ladle of batter and swirl or spread thin, covering and cooking until the top is set and small holes form.
Serve warm, often with honey or stew.

dishes.name: Bariis Iskukaris
dishes.description: Somali spiced rice dish, often served at gatherings.
steps: Rinse the basmati rice under cold water until it runs mostly clear, then soak for 20-30 minutes and drain well.
Heat oil or ghee in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add whole spices (cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, cloves) and toast for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add sliced onion and cook for 6-8 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the xawaash spice blend and tomato paste, cooking for 1-2 minutes to bloom the spices and deepen their flavor.
Add the drained rice to the pot and stir to coat every grain in the spiced, oniony base.
Pour in the appropriate amount of water or stock (typically about 1.5 times the volume of rice), season with salt, and bring to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce heat to the lowest setting, cover tightly, and cook undisturbed for 18-20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is fully absorbed.
Remove from heat and let it rest, covered, for 5-10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork before serving alongside meat or vegetable stew.

dishes.name: Cepelinai
dishes.description: Zeppelin-shaped Lithuanian potato dumplings stuffed with meat.
steps: Grate raw potato and squeeze out excess liquid, reserving the starch that settles.
Mix the grated potato with mashed potato and reserved starch to form a dough.
Mix ground pork with minced onion for the filling.
Shape dough around a portion of filling into a large oval (zeppelin shape).
Boil gently until they float and the dough turns slightly translucent, about 30-40 minutes.

dishes.name: Skyr
dishes.description: Thick, protein-rich Icelandic cultured dairy product.

ingredients.name: skyr culture or plain yogurt starter

ingredient_names: skyr culture or plain yogurt starter
steps: Warm the milk gently in a heavy-bottomed pot to about 180°F (82°C), stirring occasionally to prevent scorching on the bottom — this pasteurizes it and denatures the proteins for a better set.
Let the milk cool to about 110°F (43°C) — warm to the touch but not hot. This is important, as too-hot milk will kill the culture.
Whisk in a spoonful of live skyr or plain yogurt (with active cultures) as your starter, mixing until fully combined.
Pour the mixture into a clean container, cover, and let it sit in a warm spot (like an oven with just the light on, or wrapped in towels) for 6-8 hours, or until thickened and tangy.
Once set, line a colander with cheesecloth or a thin, clean towel and set it over a bowl. Pour in the cultured milk and let the whey drain off.
Let it strain for several hours, or overnight in the fridge, until it reaches a thick, spoonable consistency — the longer it strains, the thicker and more yogurt-cheese-like it becomes.
Transfer the strained skyr to a container and refrigerate. Serve cold, plain or with fruit, honey, or granola.

dishes.name: Karjalanpiirakka
dishes.description: Karelian rice pastry with a thin rye crust, a Finnish breakfast classic.
steps: Mix rye flour with water into a thin, pliable dough.
Roll into thin ovals.
Spread cooked rice porridge in the center of each oval.
Fold and crimp the edges up around the filling, leaving the center exposed.
Bake at high heat until the edges are lightly browned, then brush with melted butter.

dishes.name: Ají de Gallina
dishes.description: Creamy Peruvian chicken stew colored and spiced by yellow chili.
steps: Sauté onion and garlic with aji amarillo paste until fragrant.
Blend the soaked bread with a little milk until smooth, then stir into the pan.
Add ground walnuts and parmesan, simmering until thickened into a creamy sauce.
Fold in the shredded chicken and warm through.
Serve over rice with sliced boiled egg and olives.

dishes.name: Causa Limeña
dishes.description: Layered chilled potato dish, molded and filled, from Lima.
steps: Mash boiled potato while warm, then mix in aji amarillo paste and lime juice.
Season with salt and let cool completely.
Press a layer of the potato mixture into a mold or dish.
Spread a layer of chicken or tuna salad filling on top.
Top with another layer of potato, chill, then unmold and slice to serve.

dishes.name: Anticuchos
dishes.description: Peruvian grilled skewers, traditionally made from marinated beef heart.
steps: Trim the meat (traditionally beef heart, though sirloin works too) of any excess sinew and cut into even 1-inch cubes.
Make the marinade: blend or whisk together ají panca paste (or a mix of paprika and chili powder), red wine vinegar, minced garlic, cumin, and salt into a smooth paste.
Toss the meat cubes in the marinade, making sure every piece is well coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or ideally overnight for the deepest flavor.
If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 20 minutes. Thread the marinated meat onto the skewers, a few pieces per skewer.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat. Grill the skewers for 3-4 minutes per side, basting occasionally with any extra marinade, until charred on the outside and cooked to your liking inside.
Baste one more time with a little oil mixed with ají panca just before removing from the heat for a final glossy, spicy coating.
Serve hot, traditionally with boiled potato and grilled corn on the side, plus extra ají sauce for dipping.

dishes.name: Milanesa
dishes.description: Argentine breaded and fried cutlet, similar to schnitzel.
steps: Place the meat cutlets between two sheets of plastic wrap and pound with a meat mallet or rolling pin until evenly thin, about 1/4 inch thick — this tenderizes the meat and helps it cook quickly and evenly.
Set up a breading station: one plate with flour seasoned with salt and pepper, a second bowl with beaten eggs, and a third plate with breadcrumbs.
Season the cutlets on both sides with salt, pepper, and garlic powder if using.

Dredge each cutlet first in the flour, shaking off the excess, then dip in the beaten egg, letting the excess drip off, and finally press firmly into the breadcrumbs so they adhere in an even layer on both sides.
Heat about 1/2 inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering (a breadcrumb dropped in should sizzle immediately).

Fry the breaded cutlets in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden-brown and crisp, and the meat is cooked through. Don't crowd the pan or the temperature will drop and the coating will turn greasy.
Transfer to a wire rack or paper towels to drain briefly (a rack keeps the bottom crisp better than paper towels alone).
Serve hot with lemon wedges, and a simple side salad or mashed potatoes.

dishes.name: Provoleta
dishes.description: Grilled provolone cheese, a classic starter at an Argentine asado.
steps: Place a thick slice of provolone in a small cast iron pan or directly on the grill grate over medium heat.
Sprinkle with oregano and a drizzle of olive oil.
Grill until the bottom is golden and the cheese is melted but still holding together.
Carefully flip if using a pan, or serve directly from the grill.
Serve immediately with bread for scooping.

dishes.name: Pozole
dishes.description: Traditional Mexican hominy soup, festive and deeply regional.
steps: Simmer pork shoulder in a large pot of water with garlic and onion until very tender, about 1.5-2 hours — this also builds the base broth.
While the pork cooks, toast dried guajillo chilies briefly until fragrant, then soak them in hot water until softened.
Blend the softened chilies with a little soaking water into a smooth, deep red sauce.
Once tender, remove the pork and shred it. Strain the broth if cloudy, then return it to the pot.
Stir the chili sauce into the broth, along with hominy.
Return the shredded pork and simmer everything together another 30-45 minutes to let flavors meld.
Taste and season with salt.
Serve hot with shredded cabbage, sliced radish, chopped onion, lime wedges, and dried oregano on the side for everyone to garnish their own bowl.

dishes.name: Birria
dishes.description: Rich, chili-braised meat stew, often served with tortillas for dipping tacos.
steps: Toast dried guajillo and ancho chilies briefly until fragrant, then remove stems and seeds and soak in hot water until softened, about 15-20 minutes.
Blend the softened chilies with garlic, a little vinegar, and warming spices into a smooth, thick marinade.
Coat beef or goat chunks thoroughly in the marinade.
Transfer the meat and marinade to a large pot, add enough water or stock to mostly cover, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer very gently for 2.5-3 hours, checking occasionally, until the meat is completely falling-apart tender.
Once tender, remove and shred the meat with two forks.
Strain the cooking liquid — this becomes your consommé, a rich broth for dipping.
Dip tortillas in the fatty top layer of the consommé before griddling, then fill with shredded meat and a little cheese, folding into tacos and griddling until crisp on both sides.
Serve the crispy tacos alongside small cups of hot consommé for dipping.

dishes.name: Elote
dishes.description: Grilled Mexican street corn slathered in creamy, spiced toppings.
steps: Preheat a grill, grill pan, or broiler to high heat. Shuck 4 ears of corn, removing all the husks and silk.
Grill the corn directly over the heat, turning every 2-3 minutes, for about 10-12 minutes total, until it's tender and charred in spots on all sides.
While the corn grills, stir the mayonnaise (or crema) in a small bowl to loosen it slightly.
Once the corn is done, brush or spread each ear generously with the mayonnaise while it's still hot, so it slightly melts into the kernels.
Sprinkle the mayonnaise-coated corn generously with the crumbled cotija cheese, then dust with 1 tablespoon chili powder, distributing it evenly over all 4 ears.
Squeeze fresh lime juice over the top just before serving, and eat immediately while hot.

dishes.name: Chilaquiles
dishes.description: Mexican breakfast of fried tortilla chips simmered in salsa.
steps: If making your own tortilla chips, cut corn tortillas into triangles and fry until crisp and golden, then drain.
Warm your salsa in a large pan until simmering gently, not boiling hard.
Add the crispy chips to the pan with the salsa.

Toss the chips in the salsa quickly and gently, just until coated and slightly softened — this has to be fast, since the whole point is chips that are saucy but still have some crunch, not fully soggy.
Transfer to a plate immediately once coated.
Top with crumbled queso fresco and a drizzle of crema.
Fry an egg separately, sunny-side up, and place on top.
Serve immediately while the chips still have texture, garnished with sliced onion and cilantro.

dishes.name: Tamales
dishes.description: Steamed corn dough parcels filled with meat, cheese, or chilies.
steps: Soak dried corn husks in warm water for at least 30 minutes until pliable enough to fold without cracking.
Beat lard or shortening until light and fluffy using a mixer — this aeration is what gives the masa a light, tender texture rather than dense and heavy.

Gradually mix in masa harina and broth, alternating between them, until you have a soft, spreadable dough about the consistency of thick peanut butter. Test readiness by dropping a small ball into a cup of water — if it floats, it's aerated enough.
Prepare your filling of choice.
Spread a thin, even layer of masa over about two-thirds of a softened corn husk, leaving a border.
Add a spoonful of filling in a line down the center of the masa.
Fold one long side of the husk over the filling, then the other, so the masa encloses it, then fold up the empty tapered end.
Stand the folded tamales upright in a steamer basket, open-end up, packing them snugly so they support each other.
Steam over simmering water for about 1-1.5 hours, checking the water level periodically.
Check doneness by unwrapping one — the masa should pull cleanly away from the husk; if sticky, steam longer.
Let tamales rest a few minutes before serving to firm up.

dishes.name: Mofongo
dishes.description: Mashed fried plantain dish, a Puerto Rican signature.
steps: Peel green plantains and cut them into thick chunks.
Heat oil for frying and fry the plantain at a lower temperature first, about 300°F (150°C), for several minutes until softened but only lightly colored.
Remove and let cool slightly, then increase the oil to 350°F (175°C) for a second, hotter fry that crisps the outside, about 2-3 minutes more.
While still warm, transfer the fried plantain to a mortar along with minced garlic and a bit of the frying oil.
Mash everything together vigorously — this takes real physical effort, working the plantain into a cohesive, slightly sticky mash.
Mix in crumbled pork cracklings, continuing to mash until well combined.
Pack the mashed mixture into a dome shape, either by hand or using the mortar as a mold, then turn out onto a plate.
Serve warm, often with garlic sauce or a light broth poured around the base to keep it moist.

dishes.name: Arroz con Gandules
dishes.description: Puerto Rico's classic rice and pigeon pea dish.
steps: Heat a little oil in a large pot with a tight-fitting lid over medium heat. Add 1/2 cup sofrito and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until fragrant.
Add 1/4 cup tomato sauce and the pigeon peas, and cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, to let the flavors combine.
Add 3 cups rice to the pot and stir well so every grain gets coated in the sofrito-tomato mixture.
Pour in water (typically about 1.5 times the volume of rice, so around 4.5 cups - check your rice package for the exact ratio), and stir once to combine. Season with salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover tightly, and cook without lifting the lid or stirring for 20-25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is fully absorbed.
Remove from heat, fold in 1/4 cup olives, then let it rest, covered, for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork and serving.

dishes.name: Conch Fritters
dishes.description: Deep-fried fritters made from local conch, a Bahamian favorite.
steps: Tenderize the conch meat by pounding it with a meat mallet, then finely dice or pulse briefly in a food processor until it's in small, even pieces.
In a bowl, combine the diced conch with finely diced bell pepper, onion, celery, and minced garlic.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, a pinch of cayenne, salt, and pepper. Add an egg and just enough milk or water to form a thick batter that will hold together.
Fold the conch and vegetable mixture into the batter until evenly combined — the mixture should be thick enough to hold its shape when scooped.
Heat about 2-3 inches of oil in a deep, heavy pot to 350°F (175°C).
Drop rounded spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil, a few at a time so the temperature doesn't drop too much.
Fry for 3-4 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden-brown on all sides and cooked through in the center.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with a spicy dipping sauce, such as a mix of mayonnaise, lime juice, and hot sauce.

dishes.name: Kokoda
dishes.description: Fijian version of ceviche, fish cured in citrus and coconut milk.
steps: Use only very fresh, sushi-grade or otherwise trustworthy white fish, since it will be 'cooked' by the acid in the lime rather than heat. Cut it into small, even cubes, about 1/2 inch.
Place the cubed fish in a glass or ceramic bowl (avoid reactive metal bowls) and pour over 1/2 cup lime juice, making sure all the fish is submerged or well coated.
Cover and refrigerate for 15-20 minutes, checking partway through - the fish is ready when it turns opaque and firm all the way through, similar to how it looks when cooked with heat.
Drain off about half of the lime juice, leaving just enough to keep things moist.
Gently fold in 1 cup coconut milk, the diced tomato, diced onion, and minced chili.
Chill for another 5-10 minutes to let the flavors combine, then serve cold, straight from the bowl.

dishes.name: Palusami
dishes.description: Taro leaves baked with coconut cream, a Samoan staple.
steps: Layer several taro leaves together to prevent tearing.
Spoon coconut cream and diced onion (and meat if using) into the center.
Fold the leaves tightly around the filling into a parcel.
Wrap in foil or additional leaves and bake or steam for about an hour.
Unwrap and serve the softened, creamy filling with rice.

dishes.name: Beignets
dishes.description: Square, pillowy fried dough dusted heavily with powdered sugar.
steps: In a bowl, dissolve the yeast and a pinch of sugar in warm water and let sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, remaining sugar, and salt. Add the yeast mixture, evaporated milk, egg, and melted butter, mixing until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms.
Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface for about 5 minutes until smooth and elastic. Place in an oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place for about 1.5-2 hours, or until doubled.
Roll the risen dough out on a floured surface to about 1/4-inch thickness. Cut into roughly 2x3-inch rectangles with a knife or pizza cutter.
Heat about 3 inches of oil in a deep, heavy pot to 360°F (182°C). Fry the dough pieces in small batches for 2-3 minutes, flipping once, until puffed and golden-brown on both sides.
Drain on paper towels or a wire rack for a minute, then generously dust with powdered sugar while still hot — pile it on, this is not the place to hold back.
Serve immediately while warm and fresh; beignets are best eaten right away, ideally with coffee.

dishes.name: Fish Tacos
dishes.description: Crispy battered fish tacos, a Baja California classic adopted widely in the US.
steps: Cut the fish fillets into strips about 1 inch wide.

Heat a couple inches of oil in a deep pot or heavy skillet to 350°F (175°C) - if you don't have a thermometer, test by dropping in a small bit of batter; it should sizzle and rise to the surface within a few seconds.
Pat the fish strips dry, then dip each one into the beer batter, letting the excess drip off.

Carefully lower the battered fish into the hot oil, a few pieces at a time so the pan isn't crowded. Fry for 3-4 minutes, turning once, until golden brown and crisp on the outside and cooked through (opaque and flaky) inside.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Warm the corn tortillas in a dry skillet for about 20 seconds per side, or wrapped in foil in a low oven.
Fill each warm tortilla with a piece of fried fish and a handful of cabbage slaw, then drizzle with crema and a squeeze of fresh lime juice. Serve immediately.

dishes.name: Cobb Salad
dishes.description: Composed American salad with rows of chopped toppings.
steps: Arrange chopped lettuce as a base on a large platter.
Arrange rows of diced chicken, crumbled bacon, sliced egg, blue cheese, and diced avocado across the top.
Add halved cherry tomatoes for color.
Keep the toppings in neat rows rather than tossed.
Serve with a vinaigrette on the side, tossed together just before eating.

dishes.name: Apple Pie
dishes.description: Classic American baked pie, a cultural symbol as much as a dessert.
steps: Make the crust first so it has time to chill: combine 2.5 cups of flour with a pinch of salt, then cut in very cold, cubed butter using a pastry cutter or your fingers, working quickly until it looks like coarse crumbs with pea-sized butter pieces still visible — those bits are what make the crust flaky, so don't overwork it.
Add ice water a tablespoon at a time, mixing gently just until the dough comes together when pressed. Divide into two discs, wrap, and refrigerate at least an hour.

Peel and slice 6 apples into even, thin slices. Toss in a bowl with sugar, a teaspoon of cinnamon, and a couple tablespoons of flour — the flour thickens the juices that release as the pie bakes, so don't skip it or you'll get a soggy, watery filling.

On a floured surface, roll out one disc into a circle a couple inches wider than your pie dish. Transfer it by rolling loosely around your rolling pin, then unrolling over the dish — this prevents tearing.
Press the dough gently into the corners without stretching it (stretched dough shrinks back during baking).
Pour in the apple filling, mounding it slightly in the center since apples shrink as they cook.
Roll out the second disc and place over the filling. Trim the excess overhang to about an inch, fold the edges under, and crimp with your fingers or a fork to seal.
Cut a few small slits in the top crust — this lets steam escape, preventing the top from ballooning or the filling from bursting out the sides.
Brush the top with beaten egg or milk for a shiny finish, and sprinkle with a little extra sugar if you like.

Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 45-50 minutes. If the edges brown too quickly, loosely cover them with foil partway through. It's done when the crust is deep golden and you can see the filling bubbling through the slits.
Let the pie cool for at least 2 hours before slicing — cutting too soon means the filling runs out watery instead of holding together.

dishes.name: Biscuits and Gravy
dishes.description: Southern breakfast of flaky biscuits smothered in peppery sausage gravy.
steps: Make flaky buttermilk biscuits and bake until golden.
Brown breakfast sausage in a skillet, breaking it into crumbles.
Sprinkle flour over the sausage and cook briefly to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk, simmering until thick and peppery.
Split warm biscuits and ladle the sausage gravy generously over the top.

dishes.name: Cornbread
dishes.description: Slightly sweet, crumbly baked bread made from cornmeal.
steps: Whisk together cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk buttermilk, egg, and melted butter.
Combine the wet and dry ingredients just until mixed.
Pour into a greased pan or hot skillet.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20-25 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.

dishes.name: Polenta
dishes.description: Creamy or firm cornmeal porridge, a staple of Northern Italian cuisine.
steps: Bring water or stock to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pot (about 4 cups liquid per cup of polenta), adding a generous pinch of salt.
Reduce the heat to a gentle simmer and slowly pour in the polenta (cornmeal) in a thin, steady stream while whisking constantly — this prevents lumps from forming.
Once all the polenta is incorporated and the mixture starts to thicken, switch to a wooden spoon and reduce the heat to low.

Cook, stirring frequently (every minute or two) to prevent sticking and scorching on the bottom, for 30-40 minutes for traditional coarse polenta, or 5-10 minutes if using quick-cooking polenta — it's ready when thick, creamy, and no longer gritty on the tongue.
Stir in butter and grated parmesan cheese, mixing until melted and glossy. Taste and adjust salt.

Serve immediately while soft and creamy, spooned into bowls and topped with a stew, mushrooms, or a fried egg — or, for a firmer style, pour it into a dish, let it cool and set, then slice and pan-fry or grill later.

dishes.name: Osso Buco
dishes.description: Braised veal shanks, traditionally finished with a lemon-herb gremolata.
steps: Dredge veal shanks in flour and brown well on all sides.
Sauté diced carrot, celery, and onion in the same pot until softened.
Return the shanks, add white wine and enough stock to come partway up the sides.
Cover and braise at 325°F (160°C) for about 2 hours until very tender.
Finish with a sprinkle of fresh gremolata before serving.

dishes.name: Yakitori
dishes.description: Grilled skewered chicken, glazed with a sweet-savory sauce.
steps: Thread chicken and scallion pieces alternately onto skewers.
Grill over charcoal or high heat, turning occasionally.
Baste repeatedly with tare sauce as it cooks, building up a glossy glaze.
Cook until the chicken is fully cooked through and lightly charred.
Serve hot, straight off the grill.

dishes.name: Unagi Don
dishes.description: Glazed grilled eel served over a bowl of rice.
steps: If the unagi (grilled eel) is frozen or pre-cooked, thaw it if needed, then warm it gently: brush with its accompanying sauce and grill or broil for 3-4 minutes per side, basting once more, until glossy and lightly caramelized at the edges. If pan-searing instead, warm skin-side down first in a lightly oiled pan for 2-3 minutes, then flip.
While the eel warms, cook the rice: rinse until the water runs mostly clear, then cook according to package directions (typically a 1:1.1 rice-to-water ratio) until tender and glossy.
Spoon the hot cooked rice into serving bowls, packing it gently so it's level.
Slice the warm unagi into strips and lay it over the rice, overlapping the pieces slightly to cover the surface.
Drizzle any extra unagi sauce (a sweet soy-based glaze) generously over the top — don't skimp, since it flavors the rice underneath too.
Finish with a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds and thin strips of nori, and serve immediately while the eel is warm and glossy.

dishes.name: Crème Brûlée
dishes.description: Rich custard dessert topped with a brittle layer of caramelized sugar.
steps: Warm cream with a scraped vanilla bean until just simmering.
Whisk egg yolks with sugar until pale, then slowly temper in the warm cream.
Strain and pour into ramekins.
Bake in a water bath at 325°F (160°C) until just set with a slight jiggle, about 35-40 minutes.
Chill, then sprinkle sugar on top and caramelize with a torch just before serving.

dishes.name: Profiteroles
dishes.description: Cream-filled pastry puffs drizzled with warm chocolate sauce.
steps: Make the choux pastry: bring water and butter to a boil in a saucepan. Remove from heat and dump in the flour all at once, stirring vigorously until it forms a smooth ball that pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Return the pan to low heat and cook, stirring, for 1-2 minutes to dry out the dough slightly. Transfer to a bowl and let cool for 5 minutes (so it doesn't scramble the eggs).
Beat in the eggs one at a time, mixing thoroughly after each addition, until you have a smooth, glossy dough that falls off the spoon in a thick ribbon.
Pipe or spoon the dough into small rounds (about 1.5 inches) onto a parchment-lined baking sheet, spacing them a couple inches apart. Smooth any peaks with a wet finger.

Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20-25 minutes until puffed and deep golden-brown — resist opening the oven early or they may collapse. Pierce each puff with a small knife right out of the oven to let steam escape, then let cool completely on a wire rack.
Once cool, slice the puffs in half or use a piping bag to fill them with whipped cream through a small hole in the base.
Arrange the filled puffs on a serving plate and drizzle generously with warm chocolate sauce just before serving, so the puffs stay crisp.

dishes.name: Panna Cotta
dishes.description: Silky Italian set cream dessert, often served with fruit or caramel.
steps: Pour a few tablespoons of cold milk or cream into a small bowl and sprinkle the gelatin evenly over the surface. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes to bloom (soften and absorb the liquid) — this prevents lumps later.

In a saucepan, combine the remaining cream, milk, sugar, and a split vanilla bean (or vanilla extract) over medium heat. Warm gently, stirring occasionally, until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is steaming but not boiling.
Remove from heat and whisk in the bloomed gelatin until it's fully dissolved and the mixture is smooth — make sure no gelatin granules remain.
If you used a vanilla bean, strain the mixture through a fine sieve to remove the pod, then stir the scraped seeds back in.
Divide the mixture evenly among small ramekins or glasses. Let cool to room temperature, then cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or until fully set and just barely wobbly.
To unmold, dip each ramekin briefly in warm water for a few seconds to loosen the edges, then invert onto a plate — or simply serve in the glasses if you prefer.
Top with fresh berries, a fruit coulis, or a drizzle of caramel just before serving.

dishes.name: Cannoli
dishes.description: Sicilian fried pastry tubes filled with sweetened ricotta.
steps: Place the drained ricotta in a fine-mesh strainer lined with cheesecloth set over a bowl, and let it drain in the refrigerator for at least an hour (or longer) to remove as much excess liquid as possible - wet ricotta will make a runny filling.
Transfer the well-drained ricotta to a mixing bowl and add 1/2 cup powdered sugar.
Whip the mixture with a whisk or electric mixer for 2-3 minutes, until it's smooth, light, and no longer grainy.
Fold in 1/4 cup mini chocolate chips gently with a spatula, distributing them evenly throughout the filling.
Spoon the filling into a piping bag (or a zip-top bag with the corner snipped off), and pipe it into both ends of each cannoli shell, filling them completely.
Fill the shells just before serving, not too far ahead of time, since the shells will soften and lose their crunch if filled too early. Dust with a little extra powdered sugar before serving.

dishes.name: Gelato
dishes.description: Dense, intensely flavored Italian frozen dessert.
steps: Warm milk and cream together until steaming.
Whisk egg yolks with sugar, then temper in the warm milk mixture.
Cook gently over low heat, stirring, until the mixture thickens slightly to coat a spoon.
Chill the base completely, then churn in an ice cream maker.
Freeze until firm, softening slightly before serving.

dishes.name: Macaron
dishes.description: Delicate almond meringue sandwich cookies in bright colors.
steps: Sift almond flour and powdered sugar together.
Whip egg whites to soft peaks, then gradually add granulated sugar to stiff, glossy peaks.
Fold the almond mixture into the meringue until it flows in a thick ribbon.
Pipe small rounds onto a lined baking sheet and let rest until a skin forms, about 30 minutes.
Bake at 300°F (150°C) until they develop feet and are set, about 15 minutes, then sandwich with filling.

dishes.name: Banoffee Pie
dishes.description: British pie layering banana, toffee, and cream over a biscuit crust.
steps: Make (or buy) a biscuit crust: pulse about 250g digestive biscuits to fine crumbs and mix with 100g melted butter until it looks like wet sand. Press firmly and evenly into the base and up the sides of a 9-inch pie or tart dish, using the flat bottom of a glass to pack it tight.
Chill the crust in the fridge for at least 30 minutes (or freezer for 10) so it holds together when sliced.
Spread the dulce de leche or toffee evenly over the chilled crust in a thick, even layer, going right to the edges so every slice gets some.
Slice 3 bananas into rounds just before assembling (do this last-minute so they don't brown) and arrange them in an even layer over the toffee, overlapping slightly to cover the surface completely.
Whip the cream to soft-to-medium peaks — it should hold its shape but still look glossy, not grainy. Don't overwhip or it will turn stiff and buttery.
Pile the whipped cream over the bananas, swirling it into peaks with the back of a spoon rather than smoothing it flat — this gives the pie texture and makes it look more generous.
Chill the finished pie for at least 1 hour before serving so the layers set and slice cleanly.
Just before serving, dust with cocoa powder or grate dark chocolate over the top for a professional finish. Use a warm, dry knife (run under hot water and wipe) for clean slices.

dishes.name: Sticky Toffee Pudding
dishes.description: Moist date cake soaked in a rich toffee sauce, a British classic.
steps: Soak chopped dates in hot water with baking soda until softened, then blend into a puree.
Cream butter and sugar, then beat in eggs and the date puree.
Fold in flour and pour into a baking dish.
Bake at 350°F (180°C) until a skewer comes out clean, about 30-35 minutes.
Make a toffee sauce by simmering butter, brown sugar, and cream, then pour warm over the cake.

dishes.name: Mochi
dishes.description: Chewy pounded rice cakes, often filled with sweet bean paste or ice cream.
steps: Whisk glutinous rice flour, sugar, and water together until smooth.
Microwave or steam the mixture in short intervals, stirring between each, until it becomes thick and translucent.
Dust a work surface generously with cornstarch and turn out the hot dough.
Divide and flatten small portions, then wrap around a spoonful of sweet filling.
Pinch closed and dust off excess cornstarch before serving.

dishes.name: Dorayaki
dishes.description: Two small pancakes sandwiching a sweet red bean filling.
steps: Whisk eggs, honey, and sugar together, then fold in flour and a little water to make a thick pancake batter.
Rest the batter for 15 minutes.
Cook small rounds on a griddle like pancakes until golden on both sides.
Spread red bean paste generously on the flat side of one pancake.
Sandwich with a second pancake, flat sides together.

dishes.name: Gulab Jamun
dishes.description: Deep-fried milk dumplings soaked in fragrant sugar syrup.
steps: Mix milk powder, flour, and a little milk into a soft dough.
Shape into small smooth balls, taking care to avoid cracks.
Fry the balls in oil on low-medium heat until deeply golden all over, turning gently.
Make a light sugar syrup with cardamom and rosewater.
Soak the fried balls in the warm syrup for at least an hour before serving.

dishes.name: Rasgulla
dishes.description: Spongy Bengali cheese balls soaked in light syrup.
steps: Bring milk to a boil, then add lemon juice to curdle it, separating curds from whey.
Strain and rinse the curds (chenna), then knead until smooth.
Shape into small smooth balls.
Boil the balls in a light sugar syrup until they double in size and become spongy, about 15-20 minutes.
Chill in the syrup before serving.

dishes.name: Kheer
dishes.description: North Indian rice pudding, fragrant with cardamom and nuts.
steps: Simmer rice in milk over low heat, stirring occasionally, until the rice is soft and the milk has thickened considerably, about 45 minutes.
Add sugar and cardamom, stirring until dissolved.
Continue simmering until the desired creamy consistency is reached.
Fry nuts and raisins in a little ghee and stir in.
Serve warm or chilled.

dishes.name: Turkish Delight
dishes.description: Chewy, fragrant gel-based confection dusted with powdered sugar.
steps: Dissolve sugar in water and bring to a simmer.
In a separate pot, whisk cornstarch with cold water into a smooth slurry, then combine with the sugar syrup.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until it becomes very thick and translucent, about 45 minutes.
Stir in rosewater and pour into a greased pan to set for several hours.
Cut into squares and toss generously in powdered sugar.

dishes.name: Halva
dishes.description: Dense, sweet confection found across the Middle East, made from tahini or semolina.
steps: Heat sugar and water together until it reaches a thick syrup stage.
Warm the tahini slightly so it's pourable.
Combine the hot syrup with the tahini, stirring vigorously until it starts to thicken.
Pour into a lined pan and press down firmly.
Let it cool and set completely before slicing into pieces.

dishes.name: Basbousa
dishes.description: Sweet semolina cake soaked in syrup, popular across the Arab world.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a baking pan.
In a large bowl, whisk together the semolina, sugar, and shredded coconut. Stir in the yogurt and melted butter, mixing until you have a thick, even batter.
Let the batter rest for 10-15 minutes so the semolina can absorb some of the moisture and soften slightly — this helps the final texture.

Spread the batter evenly into the prepared pan, smoothing the top with a spatula. Score the surface into diamond or square shapes with a knife, cutting about halfway through (this makes it easy to portion once baked and soaked).
If you like, press a whole almond into the center of each scored piece for a traditional finishing touch.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, until the top is golden-brown and a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
While the cake bakes, make the sugar syrup: simmer sugar and water together with a squeeze of lemon juice for 5-8 minutes until slightly thickened, then let it cool.
As soon as the basbousa comes out of the oven, pour the cooled syrup evenly over the hot cake — pouring cold syrup over hot cake (or vice versa) helps it absorb evenly without turning soggy.
Let it sit for at least 30 minutes to fully soak up the syrup before cutting along the scored lines and serving.

dishes.name: Flan
dishes.description: Silky caramel custard popular across Spain and Latin America.
steps: Melt sugar in a pan until it turns a deep amber caramel, then pour into a baking dish, swirling to coat the bottom.
Whisk eggs, condensed milk, and evaporated milk together until smooth.
Pour the custard over the caramel.
Bake in a water bath at 350°F (180°C) for about 45-50 minutes until set.
Chill completely, then invert onto a plate so the caramel becomes a sauce.

dishes.name: Tres Leches Cake
dishes.description: Sponge cake soaked in a blend of three milks until fully saturated.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9x13-inch baking pan.
Whisk together flour, baking powder, and a pinch of salt in a bowl. In a separate bowl, beat eggs and sugar until pale and fluffy, then mix in vanilla extract.
Gently fold the dry ingredients into the egg mixture in batches, alternating with milk, mixing just until combined — don't overmix, or the cake will turn dense.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and spread evenly. Bake for 25-30 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean and the top springs back when touched.
Let the cake cool in the pan for about 10 minutes, then poke holes all over the top with a fork or skewer, spacing them fairly close together.
Whisk together the three milks — evaporated milk, sweetened condensed milk, and whole milk (or heavy cream) — until well combined.
Slowly pour the milk mixture evenly over the warm cake, letting it soak in gradually rather than pooling on top — pour a little, wait, then pour more.
Refrigerate the soaked cake for at least 2-3 hours, or ideally overnight, so it fully absorbs the milk mixture and becomes rich and moist throughout.
Just before serving, whip cream with a little sugar to soft peaks and spread over the top of the cake, finishing with a dusting of cinnamon or fresh fruit if you like.

dishes.name: Dulce de Leche
dishes.description: Thick, caramelized milk spread, central to Argentine desserts.
steps: Combine milk, sugar, baking soda, and vanilla in a heavy pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally.
Continue simmering for 1.5-2 hours, stirring more frequently as it thickens, until deeply caramel-colored and thick.
Watch closely near the end to prevent scorching.
Cool completely; it will thicken further as it cools.

dishes.name: Koeksisters
dishes.description: Braided fried dough soaked in cold syrup for a crisp, sticky finish.
steps: Make a soft yeasted dough and let it rise for about an hour.
Roll out and cut into strips, braiding three strips together for each koeksister.
Deep fry the braided dough until golden and cooked through.
Immediately dunk the hot fried dough into very cold sugar syrup.
Let soak briefly, then drain and serve.

dishes.name: Eggs Benedict
dishes.description: Poached eggs over muffin and ham, topped with buttery hollandaise sauce.
steps: Start the hollandaise: whisk 3 egg yolks with a tablespoon of water in a heatproof bowl set over a pot of barely simmering water (don't let the bowl touch the water). Whisk constantly for 3-4 minutes until pale, thick, and doubled in volume.

Remove from heat and very slowly drizzle in melted butter while whisking constantly, adding it a little at a time so the sauce emulsifies rather than splitting. Season with lemon juice, salt, and a pinch of cayenne. Keep warm off the heat, whisking occasionally.
Toast the English muffins until golden and crisp, then keep warm.
If using Canadian bacon or ham, warm it in a skillet over medium heat for 1-2 minutes per side until lightly browned.

Poach the eggs: bring a pot of water to a gentle simmer, add a splash of vinegar, and swirl the water into a gentle whirlpool. Slide each egg in carefully and poach for about 3 minutes until the white is set but the yolk stays runny. Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on a paper towel.
Assemble immediately: place the toasted muffin halves on plates, top each with the warmed ham, then a poached egg.

Spoon the warm hollandaise generously over each egg and finish with a crack of black pepper and a sprinkle of paprika or chives. Serve right away, while the hollandaise is warm and the yolk is still runny.

dishes.name: American Pancakes
dishes.description: Fluffy stacked griddle cakes, usually served with butter and syrup.
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together 2 cups of flour, 2 tablespoons of sugar, 2 teaspoons of baking powder, and a pinch of salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk 1.5 cups of milk with 2 eggs and a couple tablespoons of melted (not hot) butter.

Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Stir gently just until combined — flour streaks should disappear, but the batter should still look a little lumpy. Overmixing here is the number one reason pancakes turn out tough instead of fluffy, so stop as soon as you don't see dry flour.
Let the batter rest for 5 minutes while your pan heats — this gives the baking powder a moment to start working.
Heat a griddle over medium heat. Test it's ready by flicking a drop of water onto the surface — it should sizzle and dance, not sit still or evaporate instantly.
Lightly grease the pan. Pour about a third of a cup of batter per pancake, leaving space between them since they'll spread.
Watch the surface: after 2-3 minutes, small bubbles will form and pop across the top, and the edges will look matte and dry rather than wet. That's your signal to flip — not a fixed time.
Flip once, firmly and confidently. Cook the second side for another 1-2 minutes until golden.
Transfer to a plate and keep warm while you cook the rest — don't stack them right away while steaming hot, or they'll get soggy.
Serve warm with butter and maple syrup.

dishes.name: French Toast
dishes.description: Bread soaked in egg custard and pan-fried until golden.
steps: Use bread that's slightly stale or day-old if possible — fresh, soft bread tends to fall apart when soaked. Fresh bread works too, just soak it a little less.
In a shallow dish, whisk together 3 eggs, three-quarters of a cup of milk, and a teaspoon of cinnamon until fully combined with no streaks of egg remaining.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and add a pat of butter, letting it melt and coat the surface.

Dip a slice of bread into the egg mixture, letting it sit about 10-15 seconds per side — long enough to soak in, but not so long it becomes soggy and falls apart when lifted. Let excess drip off before moving it to the pan.
Place the soaked bread in the hot, buttered pan. Cook 2-3 minutes per side, until deep golden-brown — resist checking too early, a proper golden crust needs a little patience.
Flip once the first side is browned, and cook the second side the same way.
Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining slices, adding a little more butter between batches.
Serve immediately while hot, with butter, maple syrup, or fresh fruit.

dishes.name: Huevos Rancheros
dishes.description: Fried eggs served over tortillas with a spiced tomato sauce.
steps: Warm the corn tortillas one at a time in a dry skillet over medium heat, about 20-30 seconds per side, until pliable and lightly toasted. Stack them under a clean towel to stay warm.
In a small saucepan, gently heat the refried beans over low heat, stirring occasionally and adding a splash of water if they seem too thick, until warmed through and spreadable.
Spread a generous layer of warm refried beans over each tortilla, dividing it evenly among all 4.

Heat a lightly oiled nonstick skillet over medium heat. Crack each egg into the pan and cook for 2-3 minutes, until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny (or longer, if you prefer firmer yolks).
Carefully place a fried egg on top of the beans on each tortilla.
Warm the salsa ranchera in a small pot for a minute or two, then spoon it generously over the eggs on each plate. Serve immediately while everything is hot.

dishes.name: Scottish Porridge
dishes.description: Simple, traditional Scottish oatmeal, often eaten with just a pinch of salt.
steps: Bring water or milk to a gentle boil.
Stir in oats and a pinch of salt.
Reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, for about 5-10 minutes until thickened to your liking.
Let it rest a minute off the heat before serving.
Serve simply, traditionally with just a little extra salt, or with milk and a touch of sugar.

dishes.name: Muesli
dishes.description: Raw oat and fruit breakfast cereal, developed by a Swiss physician.
steps: In a large bowl, combine the rolled oats with any nuts, seeds, and dried fruit you're using.

If you like a lightly toasted flavor, spread the oats and nuts on a baking sheet and toast at 325°F (160°C) for 8-10 minutes, stirring once, until fragrant and just golden — watch closely as nuts burn quickly. Let cool completely before mixing with dried fruit (adding fruit before toasting can burn it).
Mix everything together thoroughly so the ingredients are evenly distributed throughout.
Store the dry muesli mix in an airtight container or jar — it will keep well for a few weeks at room temperature.
To serve, combine a portion of muesli with milk, yogurt, or plant milk and let it sit for at least 10-15 minutes (or overnight in the fridge) so the oats soften slightly.
Top with fresh fruit, an extra spoonful of yogurt, or a drizzle of honey before eating.

dishes.name: Nachos
dishes.description: Tortilla chips loaded with melted cheese and toppings, a Tex-Mex bar staple.
steps: Preheat your oven's broiler, or set the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Spread the tortilla chips out in a single, even layer on a large baking sheet, avoiding big piles so every chip gets some toppings and melts evenly.
Scatter 2 cups shredded cheese generously and evenly over the chips, making sure to cover as much surface area as possible.
Sprinkle the sliced jalapeño over the top.
Bake or broil for 3-5 minutes, watching closely the whole time, until the cheese is fully melted, bubbling, and just starting to brown in spots - broiled cheese can burn quickly, so don't walk away.
Remove from the oven and immediately top with dollops of salsa, sour cream, and guacamole. Serve right away while hot and crisp.

dishes.name: Onion Bhaji
dishes.description: Crispy fried onion fritters, a popular Indian snack.
steps: Thinly slice the onions and place them in a large bowl. Add the gram flour (besan), cumin seeds, chili powder, turmeric, and a good pinch of salt.

Massage the salt and spices into the onions with your hands and let them sit for 5-10 minutes — the salt will draw out moisture from the onions, which helps bind the batter without needing much added water.

Add just enough water, a tablespoon at a time, to bring everything together into a thick, clumpy batter that coats the onion strands without becoming runny — you want a batter thick enough to hold its shape when dropped into oil.
Heat about 2 inches of oil in a deep, heavy pot to 350°F (175°C).
Using two spoons, drop small clusters of the onion mixture into the hot oil, a few at a time so the temperature doesn't drop.
Fry for 4-5 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden-brown and crisp all the way through — cut one open to check the onions inside are tender, not raw.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with mint or tamarind chutney, ideally right away while they're at their crispiest.

dishes.name: Pakora
dishes.description: Battered and deep-fried vegetable fritters.
steps: Thinly slice your chosen vegetables (potato, onion, spinach, or a mix) so they're no more than 1/4 inch thick, allowing them to cook through quickly.

In a mixing bowl, whisk together 1.5 cups chickpea flour, 1 teaspoon cumin, and 1 teaspoon chili powder with 3/4 cup water, whisking until you have a smooth, thick batter with no lumps (it should coat the back of a spoon).
Heat about 2 inches of oil in a deep pot or heavy skillet to 350°F (175°C) - test by dropping in a small bit of batter; it should sizzle and float within a few seconds.
Dip the vegetable slices into the batter one at a time, making sure each one is fully and evenly coated.
Carefully lower the battered vegetables into the hot oil, a few at a time so the oil temperature doesn't drop too much, and fry for 3-4 minutes, turning occasionally, until deeply golden and crisp.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Serve hot with chutney or ketchup.

dishes.name: Kachori
dishes.description: Flaky fried pastry stuffed with spiced lentils or peas.

ingredients.name: moong dal or peas, cooked and spiced

ingredient_names: moong dal or peas, cooked and spiced
steps: Make a firm dough from flour, a little oil, and water, then rest it.
Mash cooked, spiced lentils or peas for the filling.
Wrap a portion of dough around a spoonful of filling and seal, then flatten slightly.
Deep fry on low-medium heat until deep golden and flaky, taking care they cook through without burning.
Drain and serve with chutney.

dishes.name: Vada Pav
dishes.description: Mumbai's iconic potato fritter sandwich, sometimes called the Indian burger.
steps: Boil and mash the potatoes while still warm. In a pan, heat oil and add mustard seeds, letting them pop, then add curry leaves, minced ginger, garlic, and green chili, sautéing for a minute until fragrant.
Add the mashed potatoes to the pan along with turmeric and salt, mixing thoroughly until well combined. Let the mixture cool slightly, then shape into small round patties (about golf-ball sized).
Make the batter: whisk gram flour (besan) with water, a pinch of turmeric, and salt into a smooth, thick batter — it should coat the back of a spoon.
Heat about 2 inches of oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Dip each potato patty into the batter, coating it fully, then carefully lower it into the hot oil.
Fry in batches for 4-5 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden-brown and crisp on the outside. Drain on paper towels.

Slice the pav (soft bread rolls) almost in half. Spread with green chutney and tamarind chutney on the insides, tuck a fried vada into each roll, and serve hot with a side of fried green chilies if you like extra heat.

dishes.name: Bhel Puri
dishes.description: Tangy, crunchy puffed rice snack mixed with chutneys and vegetables.
steps: In a large, wide mixing bowl, combine 3 cups puffed rice with the diced onion and tomato.
Drizzle over 1/4 cup tamarind chutney and a spicy green chutney to taste, starting with less and adding more if you like it hotter.
Toss everything together quickly and thoroughly with a large spoon or your hands - work fast here, since puffed rice absorbs moisture and loses its crunch within a couple minutes.
Taste and adjust the chutney or add a pinch of salt if needed.
Transfer to serving bowls or plates immediately.
Top generously with the crunchy sev right before serving, and eat right away while everything is still crisp.

dishes.name: Pani Puri
dishes.description: Crisp hollow shells filled with spiced tangy water, eaten in one bite.
steps: If making puris from scratch, mix semolina and flour with a pinch of salt and enough water to form a stiff dough. Roll thin and cut into small rounds, then deep-fry at 375°F (190°C) until they puff up into hollow balls — store-bought puris save time and work just as well.
Boil and finely dice potatoes, and boil chickpeas or moong sprouts until tender, then let both cool completely.
In a bowl, combine the diced potato and chickpeas with chopped onion, a pinch of chaat masala, and a little salt to make the filling.

Make the tangy mint-cilantro pani (water): blend fresh mint, cilantro, green chili, ginger, and a little tamarind pulp with water, salt, and chaat masala until smooth, then strain for a clean, vibrant green liquid. Chill until cold.
If you like a sweeter contrast, also make a tamarind-date chutney by simmering tamarind pulp with jaggery or dates and water until thick and sweet-tart.

To assemble, tap a small hole in the top of each puri with your thumb, spoon in a little of the potato-chickpea filling, add a small dollop of tamarind chutney if using, then fill with the cold minty pani.
