Eat immediately in one bite — pani puri is meant to be assembled just before eating so the puri stays crisp until the moment you bite in.

dishes.name: Aloo Tikki
dishes.description: Crisp spiced potato patties, often served with chutneys.
steps: In a large bowl, combine the mashed potato with the mashed peas, 1 teaspoon cumin, and 1 teaspoon coriander. Mix well and season with salt to taste.
Divide the mixture into equal portions (about 6-8) and shape each into a small, flat, round patty about 1/2 inch thick, pressing firmly so they hold together.
Spread the breadcrumbs on a plate. Gently press each patty into the breadcrumbs on both sides, coating them lightly and evenly.
Heat a couple tablespoons of oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat until shimmering.
Carefully place the patties in the pan without crowding, and cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden-brown and crisp on the outside, and heated through in the middle.
Drain briefly on a paper towel, then serve hot with chutneys, yogurt, or as part of a chaat.

dishes.name: Zhajiangmian
dishes.description: Northern Chinese noodles tossed in a savory fermented soybean paste sauce.
steps: Heat a little oil in a wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground pork and cook, breaking it up with a spatula, for 5-6 minutes until browned and mostly cooked through.
Push the pork to one side of the pan and add a little more oil along with minced garlic and ginger, sautéing for 30 seconds until fragrant, then stir everything together.
Add the fermented soybean paste (and a spoonful of hoisin or a pinch of sugar if you like a rounder flavor) to the pan, stirring to coat the pork evenly.

Pour in a splash of water or stock to loosen the paste into a saucy consistency, and simmer over low heat for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened into a rich, glossy sauce that clings to the meat.
While the sauce simmers, bring a pot of water to a boil and cook the wheat noodles according to package directions until just tender. Drain well (don't rinse, so the sauce clings better).
Divide the hot noodles among bowls and top each with a generous scoop of the pork sauce.
Arrange julienned cucumber and sliced scallion over the top, and serve immediately with instructions to toss everything together well before eating.

dishes.name: Dan Dan Noodles
dishes.description: Sichuan noodles in a spicy, numbing chili and sesame sauce.
steps: In each serving bowl, whisk together sesame paste, chili oil, soy sauce, and a small splash of stock or hot water to loosen it into a sauce base — mixing directly in the serving bowl means it's ready the moment the noodles finish, since this dish is best served immediately.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and add ground pork along with minced preserved vegetables. Cook, breaking the pork into small crispy crumbles, for 6-8 minutes until browned.
While the pork cooks, bring a pot of water to a boil for the noodles.
Cook wheat noodles according to package directions until just tender.
As soon as the noodles are done, drain briefly and add them directly into the sauce-filled bowls.
Toss the noodles in the sauce right in the bowl until evenly coated — the sauce should look glossy and cling to the noodles, not pool at the bottom.
Top with the crispy pork mixture.
Serve immediately, mixing everything together thoroughly with chopsticks right before eating.

dishes.name: Egg Fried Rice
dishes.description: Simple wok-fried rice with egg, a foundational Chinese home dish.
steps: Use cold, day-old rice — freshly cooked rice is too moist and will turn mushy and clump in the pan. If you only have fresh rice, spread it on a tray and refrigerate uncovered for at least 30 minutes to dry it out.
Beat 3 eggs in a small bowl with a pinch of salt.
Heat a wok over high heat until very hot — this dish cooks fast and needs high heat to avoid becoming soggy.

Add oil, then pour in the beaten eggs. Let them sit a few seconds to start setting, then scramble quickly into large, soft curds — don't overcook them, since they'll cook a little more later. Remove to a plate.
Add a bit more oil to the same wok. Break up the cold rice with your hands before adding it, separating any clumps.
Stir-fry the rice, pressing and tossing it against the hot pan, for 3-4 minutes until heated through and grains separate with light golden color in spots.
Return the scrambled egg to the pan along with chopped scallion.
Drizzle soy sauce around the edges of the pan (not directly on top) so it sizzles before mixing in — this toasts the soy sauce and deepens flavor.
Toss everything together over high heat another minute until well combined.
Serve immediately while hot.

dishes.name: Baozi
dishes.description: Fluffy steamed buns filled with savory or sweet fillings.
steps: Make a soft yeasted dough and let it rise until doubled.
Mix ground pork with scallion, ginger, and seasoning for the filling.
Roll dough into small rounds and place a spoonful of filling in the center.
Pleat and twist the top closed to seal.
Steam for 15-18 minutes until puffed and cooked through.

dishes.name: Youtiao
key_ingredients: eaten with soy milk or congee
dishes.description: Long, airy fried dough stick, a classic Chinese breakfast food.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, and baking soda with water into a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Let the dough rest for at least an hour, or ideally overnight, covered.
Roll out and cut into strips, stacking two strips together and pressing a chopstick down the middle to join them.
Stretch each pair gently and drop into hot oil.
Fry, turning frequently, until puffed, golden, and hollow inside.

dishes.name: Scallion Pancake
dishes.description: Flaky, layered savory pancake studded with scallions.
steps: Mix flour with boiling water to form a dough, then knead until smooth and rest it.
Roll the dough thin, brush with sesame oil, and scatter chopped scallion over the surface.
Roll the dough up into a log, then coil it into a spiral and flatten again.
Roll the coiled dough flat once more into a round.
Pan-fry in oil until golden and crisp on both sides, with visible flaky layers.

dishes.name: Kimbap
dishes.description: Korean seaweed rice rolls, similar to sushi but seasoned differently.

ingredients.name: cooked rice, seasoned with sesame oil
egg, cooked into a thin sheet

ingredient_names: cooked rice, seasoned with sesame oil
egg, cooked into a thin sheet
steps: Prepare and lightly season rice with sesame oil and a pinch of salt.
Lay a seaweed sheet on a bamboo mat and spread rice evenly, leaving a border at the top.
Arrange strips of carrot, pickled radish, spinach, and egg across the center.
Roll tightly using the mat, sealing the border with a little water.
Slice into rounds with a sharp knife.

dishes.name: Korean Fried Chicken
dishes.description: Extra-crispy double-fried chicken, often coated in a sweet-spicy glaze.
steps: Cut chicken wings at the joint if not already separated. Pat them completely dry — essential for crispiness.
Toss the chicken in a light, even coating of cornstarch — cornstarch, not flour, is what gives the distinctively shattering crisp texture.
Heat oil to 350°F (175°C) in a deep pot.
Fry the chicken in batches for about 8-10 minutes until cooked through and lightly golden — this first fry is mainly about cooking through, not full crispness yet.
Remove and let the chicken rest on a rack for about 10 minutes — this resting period between fries is key to the uniquely crisp coating.
Increase the oil temperature to 375°F (190°C).
Fry the chicken a second time for 3-5 minutes, until deeply golden and audibly crisp when tapped.
While it does its second fry, make the sauce: combine gochujang, minced garlic, honey, and a splash of soy sauce in a saucepan, warming gently until glossy.
As soon as the chicken comes out, toss it in the warm sauce while still hot — hot chicken absorbs the sticky glaze much better.
Serve immediately, ideally with pickled radish on the side.

dishes.name: Naengmyeon
dishes.description: Chilled buckwheat noodles in icy broth, a refreshing summer dish.
steps: Chill beef broth thoroughly, seasoning with a little vinegar and sugar.
Cook buckwheat noodles briefly, then rinse under cold water until fully chilled.
Divide noodles into bowls and pour the icy broth over them.
Top with sliced cucumber, pear, and boiled egg.
Serve immediately with a drizzle of mustard and vinegar to taste.

dishes.name: Bánh Cuốn
dishes.description: Delicate steamed rice rolls filled with seasoned pork and mushroom.
steps: Cook ground pork with minced mushroom and seasoning for the filling.
Steam a thin layer of rice batter on a cloth stretched over boiling water until set.
Scrape off the thin sheet and place a spoonful of filling in the center.
Roll gently into a soft parcel.
Serve with fried shallots and dipping sauce.

dishes.name: Cơm Tấm
dishes.description: Broken rice served with grilled pork, a beloved Saigon dish.
steps: Marinate pork chops in fish sauce, garlic, and a little sugar for at least 30 minutes.
Grill the pork chops until charred and cooked through.
Cook broken rice separately.
Serve the grilled pork over the rice with pickled vegetables on the side.
Drizzle with a light fish sauce dressing before eating.

dishes.name: Chin Chin
dishes.description: Crunchy, lightly sweet fried dough snack, common at Nigerian celebrations.
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, a pinch of salt, and nutmeg (or ground ginger, if using).
Rub in the cold butter with your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.

Make a well in the center and add the beaten eggs and a splash of milk. Mix, then knead by hand for 5-8 minutes until you have a smooth, firm dough that isn't sticky (add a little more flour if needed).
Cover the dough and let it rest for 15-20 minutes — this makes it easier to roll and helps the chin chin hold its shape.
Roll the dough out on a floured surface to about 1/4-inch thickness. Cut into small strips, then cut those strips into small squares or rectangles (roughly 1/2 to 1 inch).
Heat about 2-3 inches of oil in a deep, heavy pot to 325-350°F (165-175°C) — a lower, steadier temperature helps the chin chin cook through without burning on the outside.
Fry the pieces in batches, stirring occasionally, for 6-8 minutes until deep golden-brown and crunchy all the way through. Drain on paper towels.
Let cool completely before storing — chin chin crisps up further as it cools, and keeps well in an airtight container for a couple of weeks.

dishes.name: Puff Puff
dishes.description: Fluffy, deep-fried sweet dough balls found across West Africa.
steps: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water and let it foam.
Mix with flour into a thick, sticky batter, then let it rise for about an hour until bubbly.
Heat oil until hot.
Scoop small portions of the batter with a wet hand or spoon directly into the oil.
Fry until puffed and deeply golden all over, then drain.

dishes.name: Irio
dishes.description: Kenyan mashed dish of potatoes, corn, peas, and greens.
steps: Peel and cube 4 medium potatoes. Place them in a pot with the corn kernels and green peas, and cover with water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook for 15-20 minutes, until the potatoes are very tender when pierced with a fork.
Drain the vegetables, reserving a splash of the cooking water in case you need it later.

Return the vegetables to the pot and mash them together with a potato masher or fork, leaving some texture rather than making it perfectly smooth (some whole corn and pea pieces should remain visible).
Stir in the chopped greens and cook over low heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring, until the greens wilt and soften into the mash. Add a splash of the reserved cooking water if the mixture seems too dry.
Season with salt to taste and serve warm as a hearty side dish.

dishes.name: Bunny Chow
dishes.description: Durban curry served inside a hollowed-out loaf of bread.
steps: Cut a loaf of bread into quarters and hollow out the center of each, reserving the bread removed.
Prepare a well-spiced curry, simmered until thick.
Fill each hollowed bread quarter generously with hot curry.
Use the reserved bread as a lid or side for scooping.
Serve immediately while the curry is hot and the bread is soaking it up.

dishes.name: Musakhan
dishes.description: Palestine's national dish of sumac-spiced chicken over flatbread.
steps: Rub chicken pieces with sumac, allspice, and olive oil.
Roast or bake until golden and cooked through.
Slowly caramelize a generous amount of onion with more sumac until deep and jammy.
Spread the caramelized onion over flatbread.
Top with the roasted chicken and scatter with toasted pine nuts.

dishes.name: New England Clam Chowder
dishes.description: Creamy chowder loaded with clams and potatoes, a New England classic.
steps: If using fresh clams, steam them in a splash of water until they open, then remove the meat and chop it, reserving the flavorful steaming liquid (strain it to remove any grit). If using canned clams, drain and reserve the juice.
In a large pot, cook diced bacon or salt pork over medium heat until crisp, then remove with a slotted spoon, leaving the fat in the pot.
Sauté diced onion and celery in the bacon fat for 5-6 minutes until softened.
Sprinkle in flour and stir well to coat the vegetables, cooking for 1-2 minutes to remove the raw flour taste and form the base of the roux.
Gradually whisk in the reserved clam juice and fish or vegetable stock, stirring to keep it smooth and lump-free, then add the diced potatoes.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 15-20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Reduce the heat to low and stir in the cream (or milk), heavy cream, and the chopped clams. Warm through gently for 5 minutes — don't let it boil, as the cream can separate.
Season with salt, pepper, and a dash of Worcestershire sauce if you like. Serve hot, topped with the crispy bacon bits and a sprinkle of fresh thyme or parsley, alongside oyster crackers.

dishes.name: Key Lime Pie
dishes.description: Tart, creamy pie made from small Florida key limes.
steps: Make the crust: mix graham cracker crumbs with melted butter and a spoonful of sugar until it resembles wet sand. Press firmly into the bottom and up the sides of a 9-inch pie dish.
Bake the crust at 350°F (175°C) for 8-10 minutes until lightly golden and fragrant, then let it cool while you make the filling.
In a bowl, whisk together egg yolks and sweetened condensed milk until smooth and slightly thickened.
Gradually whisk in the fresh key lime juice (and a little zest for extra flavor), mixing until fully combined — the mixture will thicken slightly as the acid reacts with the condensed milk.
Pour the filling into the cooled crust, spreading it evenly.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 12-15 minutes, just until the filling is set around the edges but still has a slight jiggle in the center — it will continue to set as it cools.
Let the pie cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 3-4 hours, or until fully chilled and firm.
Just before serving, top with whipped cream and a few thin slices of lime for garnish.

dishes.name: S'mores
dishes.description: Campfire treat of toasted marshmallow and chocolate between graham crackers.
steps: Break graham crackers into squares and lay out chocolate pieces on half of them.
Toast marshmallows over a campfire or open flame until golden and gooey.
Place a hot marshmallow onto the chocolate-topped cracker.
Top with the second cracker and press gently to melt the chocolate.
Eat immediately while warm and gooey.

dishes.name: Kanelbulle
dishes.description: Swedish cinnamon bun, celebrated with its own national day.
steps: Make a soft yeasted dough with flour, milk, and butter, then let it rise for an hour.
Roll the dough into a large rectangle and spread with softened butter, cinnamon, and sugar.
Roll up tightly into a log and slice into rounds.
Place the rounds in muffin tins or on a baking sheet and let rise again briefly.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) until golden, about 15-18 minutes.

dishes.name: Belgian Waffles
dishes.description: Light, deep-pocketed waffles, a Belgian specialty distinct from American versions.
steps: Dissolve yeast in warm milk and let it foam.
Mix with flour, egg, and melted butter into a thick batter, then let it rise for about an hour.
Fold in pearl sugar just before cooking.
Cook in a hot waffle iron until deeply golden and the sugar caramelizes into crunchy spots.
Serve warm, plain or with toppings.

dishes.name: Tostones
dishes.description: Twice-fried green plantain slices, crispy outside and soft within.
steps: Peel the green (unripe) plantains — the skin is tough, so trim the ends first, then score the peel lengthwise and pry it off in sections. Cut the plantains into rounds about 1-inch thick.
Heat about 1 inch of oil in a skillet to 325°F (165°C). Fry the plantain rounds in batches for 3-4 minutes per side until pale golden and just tender when pierced. Remove and drain.
Once cool enough to handle, smash each piece flat to about half its original thickness using the bottom of a jar, a tostonera press, or the flat side of a knife.
Increase the oil temperature slightly to 350°F (175°C). Return the flattened plantains to the hot oil and fry a second time for 2-3 minutes per side, until crisp and golden-brown on the outside.
Drain on paper towels and season immediately with salt while still hot, so it sticks.
Serve hot as a snack or side, with a garlic mojo sauce or simply extra salt and lime for dipping.

dishes.name: Chimichurri
dishes.description: Bright, herby sauce essential to Argentine grilled meats.
steps: Finely chop 1 cup fresh parsley (leaves and thin stems) and mince 4 cloves garlic as finely as you can.
In a bowl, combine the chopped parsley, minced garlic, 1 teaspoon dried oregano, and a pinch of chili flakes if you like a little heat.
Pour in 1/4 cup red wine vinegar and stir to combine with the herbs and garlic, letting it sit for a couple minutes so the vinegar mellows the raw garlic slightly.
Slowly whisk in 3/4 cup olive oil, a little at a time, until it's well combined into a loose, spoonable sauce (it won't fully emulsify like a dressing - some separation is normal).
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Let the sauce rest at room temperature for at least 30 minutes before using, to let the flavors meld, then spoon generously over grilled meats.

dishes.name: Spam Musubi
dishes.description: Hawaiian snack of grilled spam over rice, wrapped in seaweed like sushi.
steps: Fry sliced spam until browned on both sides, then glaze with a soy-sugar mixture.
Press a layer of rice into a musubi mold (or use the empty spam can) on a strip of nori.
Top the rice with a slice of glazed spam.
Press down firmly to compact.
Wrap the nori around the rice and spam, sealing with a little water.

dishes.name: Escargot
dishes.description: Snails baked in garlic and parsley butter, a classic French starter.
steps: If using canned, pre-cleaned snails, drain and rinse them well.
Make the compound butter: mix softened butter with minced garlic, finely chopped parsley, and a pinch of salt, mashing together thoroughly.
If you have proper escargot dishes with small indentations, place a snail in each hollow with a generous spoonful of the garlic butter. Snail shells or small ramekins work as a substitute.
Top each snail generously with more garlic butter, packing it in.
Arrange the filled dishes on a baking sheet.
Bake at 425°F (220°C) for about 8-10 minutes, until the butter is fully melted and bubbling vigorously at the edges.
Serve immediately while the butter is still sizzling, with crusty bread on the side for mopping up the garlic butter.

dishes.name: Spätzle
dishes.description: Soft, irregular egg noodles, a Southern German staple.
steps: Whisk flour, eggs, milk, and a pinch of salt into a thick, elastic batter.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil.
Press the batter through a spaetzle maker or colander directly into the boiling water.
Cook until the small dumplings float, then scoop out.
Toss with melted butter, and cheese if making käsespätzle.

dishes.name: Black Pudding
dishes.description: Savory blood sausage, a traditional part of a full breakfast.
steps: Combine pork blood with oats, diced fat, and minced onion.
Season generously with black pepper and traditional spices.
Stuff the mixture into casings, or pack into a loaf-shaped mold.
Simmer gently in water until firm and cooked through.
Slice and pan-fry until crisp before serving, traditionally as part of a fry-up.

dishes.name: Cornish Pasty
dishes.description: Hand-held pastry parcel of meat and vegetables, originally miners' lunch food.
steps: Make the pastry: rub cold cubed butter (or a butter-lard mix) into flour and a pinch of salt until it resembles coarse crumbs. Add cold water gradually, mixing until a firm dough forms. Wrap and chill for at least 30 minutes.

Prepare the filling: dice the beef, potato, swede (rutabaga), and onion into small, even pieces (about 1/4-inch) so they cook through evenly inside the sealed pastry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Roll the chilled dough out on a floured surface and cut into large circles, about 8-9 inches across, using a plate as a guide.
Pile a portion of the raw filling onto one half of each circle, leaving a border around the edge, and dot with a small knob of butter for richness.
Brush the edge of the pastry with water, then fold the other half over the filling to form a half-moon shape. Press the edges together to seal.
Crimp the sealed edge by folding it over itself repeatedly along the curve (the traditional Cornish crimp), or press firmly with a fork.
Brush the pasties with beaten egg for a shiny, golden crust, and cut a small slit in the top to let steam escape.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 15 minutes, then reduce the temperature to 325°F (165°C) and bake for another 45 minutes, until deep golden-brown and the filling inside is fully cooked and tender.
Let cool for at least 10 minutes before eating, as pasties hold heat well and the filling will be very hot.

dishes.name: Welsh Rarebit
dishes.description: Savory cheese sauce spiked with mustard and ale, poured over toast.
steps: In a saucepan over low heat, melt the butter, then whisk in the flour to form a paste (a roux) and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in the beer (or milk), a little at a time, making sure each addition is smooth before adding more, to avoid lumps.
Once smooth, stir in the grated cheese a handful at a time, letting each addition melt fully before adding more, over low heat so the sauce doesn't split.
Stir in mustard powder, a dash of Worcestershire sauce, and a pinch of cayenne pepper. Cook gently for 2-3 minutes until thick, smooth, and glossy — it should coat a spoon heavily.
Toast slices of good bread until golden and firm on both sides.
Spread the hot cheese mixture generously and evenly over the toast, right to the edges.
Place under a hot broiler for 2-3 minutes, watching closely, until the top is bubbling and browned in spots.
Serve immediately while molten, with a crack of black pepper on top.

dishes.name: Crêpe
dishes.description: Thin, delicate French pancakes, sweet or savory depending on the filling.
steps: Whisk flour, eggs, milk, and melted butter into a thin, smooth batter.
Let the batter rest for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a lightly buttered crepe pan or skillet.
Pour a thin layer of batter, swirling to coat the pan, and cook until lightly golden, then flip briefly.
Fill or top with sweet or savory fillings of choice.

dishes.name: Pain au Chocolat
dishes.description: Buttery, flaky pastry wrapped around a strip of chocolate.
steps: Roll out laminated dough into a large rectangle and cut into smaller rectangles.
Place a chocolate baton near one edge of each piece and roll partway.
Add a second chocolate baton and continue rolling into a log shape.
Brush with egg wash and let proof until puffy.
Bake at 400°F (200°C) until deeply golden and flaky, about 18-20 minutes.

dishes.name: Bibim Guksu
dishes.description: Cold spicy noodles tossed in a tangy gochujang dressing.
steps: Cook thin wheat noodles until tender, then rinse under cold water until chilled.
Mix gochujang with vinegar, sugar, and sesame oil for the sauce.
Toss the cold noodles with the sauce until well coated.
Top with julienned cucumber and a halved boiled egg.
Serve cold, tossing again at the table.

dishes.name: Taiwanese Hot Pot
dishes.description: Communal simmering pot popular for gatherings, milder than Sichuan style.
steps: Bring the broth to a simmer in a pot at the center of the table.
Arrange thin-sliced meats, vegetables, and tofu on platters around the pot.
Each diner cooks their own ingredients briefly in the simmering broth.
Dip cooked items in the sesame-soy sauce before eating.
Continue adding ingredients throughout the meal, and finish with noodles in the flavorful remaining broth.

dishes.name: Durban Curry
dishes.description: Fragrant, deeply spiced curry reflecting South Africa's Indian community heritage.
steps: Prepare a richly spiced, thick lamb curry, simmered until the sauce clings to the meat.
Cut a loaf of bread into quarters and hollow out the center of each.
Fill each hollow generously with the hot curry.
Use the removed bread as a lid or side for scooping.
Serve immediately while hot, letting the bread soak up the sauce.

dishes.name: Ghanaian Rice and Beans
dishes.description: Everyday Ghanaian staple, rice and beans cooked together and colored naturally.
steps: Boil black-eyed peas with millet leaves until the peas are nearly tender and the cooking liquid turns deep red-brown.
Remove the leaves, then add rice to the same pot.
Cook covered until the rice is tender and has absorbed the color and flavor.
Fluff and serve with a side of stew.
Add gari and boiled egg alongside, as is traditional.

dishes.name: Cochinita Pibil
dishes.description: Yucatán slow-roasted pork marinated in citrus and annatto.
steps: Blend achiote paste with sour orange juice and garlic into a marinade.
Marinate the pork in this mixture for several hours or overnight.
Wrap the marinated pork tightly in banana leaves.
Slow roast at 300°F (150°C) for 3-4 hours until completely tender and shreddable.
Shred the meat and serve with pickled red onion and warm tortillas.

dishes.name: Mole Negro
dishes.description: Oaxaca's dark, complex mole sauce, deeper and smokier than mole poblano.
steps: Toast dried chilies carefully until fragrant but not burnt, then rehydrate in hot water.
Blend the chilies with tomato, plantain, and toasted spices into a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in oil, stirring constantly, until deeply darkened.
Add broth and chocolate, simmering for 45-60 minutes until thick and glossy.
Serve over poached or roasted chicken.

dishes.name: Chicken Paprikash
dishes.description: Creamy Hungarian paprika chicken stew, often served with dumplings.
steps: Season the chicken pieces with salt. Heat oil or lard in a large heavy pot over medium heat and brown the chicken on all sides, about 6-8 minutes total, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, add the diced onion and cook for 8-10 minutes over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until soft and golden — take your time here, as the onion forms the base of the sauce.
Remove the pot from direct heat briefly and stir in the sweet paprika, coating the onions well — this prevents the paprika from scorching and turning bitter, which happens quickly over direct heat.
Return to low heat and add a splash of stock to loosen the paprika-onion mixture, then return the browned chicken to the pot along with enough stock to come about halfway up the chicken.
Cover and simmer gently for 30-40 minutes, until the chicken is fully cooked and tender, turning the pieces occasionally.

Remove the chicken and keep warm. Stir a few spoonfuls of the hot cooking liquid into the sour cream to temper it (this prevents curdling), then stir the tempered sour cream back into the pot, mixing until smooth.
Warm the sauce gently over low heat (don't boil) until slightly thickened, then return the chicken to the pot to coat in the sauce.
Serve hot over nokedli (Hungarian egg dumplings) or egg noodles, with extra paprika dusted on top.

dishes.name: Zapiekanka
dishes.description: Polish open-faced baguette snack topped with mushrooms and melted cheese.
steps: Preheat your oven's broiler (or set your oven to its highest setting).

Slice the baguette in half lengthwise, then cut each half crosswise into 2-3 shorter pieces if you'd like individual portions. Place the pieces cut-side up on a baking sheet and toast lightly under the broiler for 1-2 minutes, just until they turn slightly golden - watch closely so they don't burn.
While the bread toasts, heat a splash of oil in a pan over medium heat and sauté the sliced mushrooms for 5-6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they've softened and released their liquid.
Spoon the sautéed mushrooms evenly over the toasted baguette halves.
Top generously with the shredded cheese, covering the mushrooms completely.
Return to the broiler for 3-5 minutes, watching constantly, until the cheese is fully melted, bubbling, and just starting to brown in spots. Remove, drizzle with ketchup, and serve hot.

dishes.name: Piroshki
dishes.description: Small stuffed buns, fried or baked, filled with savory or sweet fillings.
steps: Make the dough: dissolve yeast and a pinch of sugar in warm milk and let sit until foamy, about 5-10 minutes. Mix in flour, remaining sugar, salt, egg, and softened butter, kneading until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes. Let rise in a covered, oiled bowl for about an hour until doubled.

While the dough rises, make the filling: sauté diced onion until soft, add ground meat and cook through, breaking it up as it browns, then season with salt and pepper. If using cabbage or potato filling instead, cook until soft and well seasoned. Let the filling cool completely before assembling.
Punch down the risen dough and divide into 12 equal pieces. Roll each piece into a ball, then flatten into a disc about 4 inches across.
Place a spoonful of cooled filling in the center of each disc. Bring the edges up and pinch together firmly to seal into a tight seam, shaping into an oval or football shape.
Place the filled piroshki seam-side down on a baking sheet, cover loosely, and let rest for 15-20 minutes.

If baking: brush with egg wash and bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20-25 minutes until golden-brown. If frying: heat oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry seam-side down first for 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden.
Let cool slightly before serving, as the filling stays very hot.

dishes.name: Shchi
dishes.description: Traditional Russian cabbage soup, one of the country's oldest dishes.
steps: Simmer meat in water with bay leaf until tender, skimming as needed.
Add carrot and onion, cooking until softened.
Add shredded cabbage and simmer until just tender, keeping some texture.
Season with salt and a touch of vinegar or tomato for tang.
Serve hot with a dollop of sour cream and rye bread.
